## Objective

Fix step 6 by never running the agent inside the request — and get a live
progress UI as a side effect.

## Why this step exists

This is the workshop. Everything before it was setup; everything after it is
deployment. If you remember one thing:

> ### Never run the agent inside the HTTP request.

## The change

```python title="app/main.py" hl_lines="7"
@app.post("/runs", status_code=202)
async def create_run(body: RunRequest, background: BackgroundTasks):
    run_id = await db.create_run(body.query)

    # Queue the slow work to run AFTER this response has been sent.
    background.add_task(research.run_agent, run_id, body.query)

    return {"run_id": run_id, "status": "queued", "poll": f"/runs/{run_id}"}
```

- `202 Accepted` is the honest status code: *"I have taken your request, I have
   not finished it."* Not `200` — nothing is done yet.

Compare with step 6. One `await` became one `add_task`. That is the entire fix.

The response comes back in ~200 ms whether the agent takes 5 seconds or 5
minutes, because the response no longer waits for it.

Then the endpoint the client polls:

```python title="app/main.py"
@app.get("/runs/{run_id}")
async def read_run(run_id: str):
    run = await db.get_run(run_id)
    if run is None:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Run not found")
    return {"run": run, "steps": await db.get_steps(run_id)}
```

## The client side

```javascript title="client/index.html"
// 1. Ask. Comes back immediately with an id.
const response = await fetch(`${baseUrl()}/runs`, {
  method: "POST",
  headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
  body: JSON.stringify({ query }),
});
const { run_id } = await response.json();

// 2. Poll. Every 1.5s, until it's done.
pollId = setInterval(async () => {
  const poll = await fetch(`${baseUrl()}/runs/${run_id}`);
  const { run, steps } = await poll.json();

  renderSteps(steps);                       // ← the live progress
  if (run.status === "done" || run.status === "error") {
    clearInterval(pollId);
    renderResult(run);
  }
}, 1500);
```

Twenty lines. It works through every proxy, survives a phone switching networks,
and you can debug it with `curl`.

## The bonus nobody expects

You fixed a timeout problem. You also got a progress UI for free.

Because the agent writes each step to the database, every poll returns the steps
*so far*. The client doesn't just learn whether it's finished — it learns what
the agent is doing right now:

```text
✓ Planning the research
✓ Searching Wikipedia — "photovoltaic effect"
✓ Searching Wikipedia — "solar cell efficiency"
✓ Reading a source — Solar cell
⋯ Reading a source — Photovoltaics
```

The same mechanism that solved the deployment problem solved the UX problem.
That's rare enough to be worth noticing.

## Try it

From `app/`:

```bash
uv run fastapi dev main.py
```

Open `client/index.html`, **untick Naive mode**, and ask the same question as step
6.

Then run both back to back with the checkbox to feel the difference. That toggle
is the most persuasive thing in this whole project.

## Expected result

The POST returns immediately:

```json
{"run_id": "3f2a...", "status": "queued", "poll": "/runs/3f2a..."}
```

Steps appear one at a time over the next 30–60 seconds, then the answer.

Check it from the command line too:

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/runs \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"query":"how do solar panels actually work?"}'
# {"run_id":"3f2a...","status":"queued","poll":"/runs/3f2a..."}

curl http://localhost:8000/runs/3f2a...
```

**Then open the Supabase table editor and look at `steps`.** The rows are right
there. The UI is just rendering database rows — that's usually the moment this
clicks for people.

## The catch, stated honestly

`BackgroundTasks` runs **inside your server process**. If the process restarts
mid-run — a deploy, a crash, a free instance being recycled — the job vanishes
and the row sits at `running` forever.

Fine for a demo. Know it's a real limit rather than discovering it later. The
upgrade path is in
[Learn · Why deployment is hard](../../learn/deployment-problem/#the-catch-nobody-mentions),
and it doesn't change the architecture — just how the background work is
scheduled.

## A test that protects this

From `app/`:

```bash
uv run --extra dev pytest tests/test_api.py -v
```

`test_post_runs_answers_before_the_agent_has_finished` fails if anyone ever moves
the agent back inside the request. Worth keeping.

## What usually goes wrong

<details>
<summary>Steps never appear, status stays <code>queued</code></summary>


The background task isn't running or is failing instantly. Check the server
terminal — an exception in `run_agent` is caught and written to the run's
`error` column, so also check the row in Supabase.

</details>

??? failure "\"Failed to fetch\" in the browser"

    Almost always CORS. Locally, set `ALLOWED_ORIGINS=*` in `.env`. Also check
    you're not calling an `http://` backend from an `https://` page — browsers
    block that.

<details>
<summary>The run sits at <code>running</code> forever</summary>


Either the agent is genuinely still working (check `steps` for the latest
row), or the process restarted and took the task with it. That's the
`BackgroundTasks` limitation above.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Polling hammers the server</summary>


1.5 seconds is a reasonable floor. Don't go below 1s, and stop polling when
the tab is hidden if you're being careful.

</details>

## What's next

It works locally. Now put it on the internet.
